title: Assorted provider gaps found while auditing feature support
body:
While auditing feature support across the official providers, 🤖 found a few apparent bugs. I need to look into them more to confirm them.

- `chat_deepseek()` silently drops non-text user content: `as_json(Turn)` (R/provider-deepseek.R:99) keeps only `ContentText`, so images and PDFs are discarded without a warning and the model never sees them. Other providers error instead.
- `chat_snowflake()` never sets `finish_reason` in `value_turn()` (R/provider-snowflake.R:273), so the truncation warnings added in 0.4.2 (#867) can't fire. It also aborts on any content type other than text and tool use.
- `chat_aws_bedrock()` doesn't stream thinking: `stream_content()` (R/provider-aws.R:344) only emits `ContentText` live, with reasoning content only appearing in the completed turn. Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini all stream thinking, which matters for downstream use in shinychat.
- `chat_posit()` inherits `has_batch_support = TRUE` from the Anthropic provider, so `batch_chat()` will POST to `{gateway}/anthropic/v1/messages/batches` without any verification that the Posit gateway supports that endpoint.
- `google_upload()` is hardcoded to the Gemini endpoint (R/provider-google-upload.R:31), so Vertex users can't send audio or video even though the underlying models support it.

title: Model metadata omits the context window
body:
The `models_*()` functions don't report how much context a model accepts, and nothing on `Chat` exposes it either. A caller can see how many tokens a conversation has accumulated, through `get_tokens()`, but not how close that is to the limit — leaving a hardcoded per-model table that goes stale with every release, or per-provider HTTP calls, as the only ways to find out. That is the work ellmer otherwise saves callers from doing.

Most providers already return it, in a response ellmer parses and then discards. The table below is a brief overview gathered from their docs, so it may well have shifted by the time anyone acts on it.

| Provider | Endpoint | Field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic | `/v1/models` | `max_input_tokens`, `max_tokens` |
| OpenRouter | `/api/v1/models` | `context_length` |
| Gemini | `/models` | `inputTokenLimit`, `outputTokenLimit` |
| Mistral | `/v1/models` | `max_context_length` |
| vLLM | `/v1/models` | `max_model_len` |
| LM Studio | `/v1/models` | `max_context_length` |
| Ollama | `api/show` | `<arch>.context_length`, not in the `api/tags` ellmer calls |
| OpenAI | `/v1/models` | Absent |
| Bedrock | `ListFoundationModels` | Absent |
| Portkey | `/models` | Absent; normalised to the OpenAI shape before it reaches ellmer |

Five of those are a parser widening — the Anthropic parser keeps `id`, `display_name` and `created_at`, and the vLLM and LM Studio parsers keep `id` alone. Ollama needs a second call. For the last three there is nothing to read, which is what `NA` is for. OpenAI's model object is only `id`, `object`, `created` and `owned_by`, so everyone keeps their own table — including OpenAI, whose Codex CLI [added a `max_context_window` field to its own model metadata](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/18382) in April.

Suggestion: add it to the `models_*()` data frames as `max_input_tokens`, or whatever name generalises best, `NA` where the provider doesn't report it. Exposing it on `Chat` too would pair naturally with `get_tokens()`, and would give the compaction hook in #1051 the number it needs to decide.

Happy to send a PR if you'd like one.

title: chat_aws_bedrock() fails after empty response from claude-sonnet-5
body:
With `claude-sonnet-5` on Bedrock, asking the model to respond with only blank lines can produce an assistant turn with an empty thinking block and no text content. The empty thinking block is dropped by `as_json(ProviderAWSBedrock, ContentThinking)` (returns `NULL` when thinking is `""`), and `compact()` strips it, leaving `content = list()`. On the next turn, Bedrock rejects the empty content array with HTTP 400.

The fix from #376 / PR #393 handles whitespace-only `ContentText`, but this is a different case: the content array is completely empty because the only content block (empty thinking) was dropped.

## Reprex

```r
library(ellmer)
chat <- chat_aws_bedrock(model = "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5")
chat$chat("Respond with only two blank lines")
chat$chat("What's 1+1? Just give me the number")
#> Error in `req_perform()`: HTTP 400 Bad Request.
#> The content field in the Message object at messages.1 is empty.
#> Add a ContentBlock object to the content field and try again.
```

The same issue likely applies to `chat_anthropic()` since its `as_json(ProviderClaude, ContentThinking)` has the same `return()` for empty thinking.

Found while working on #1066 (bumping default models to `claude-sonnet-5`).

title: Feature request: callback before each model request in the tool loop (for mid-loop context compaction)
body:
### Summary

`Chat$chat()` / `Chat$chat_async()` (and `stream()/stream_async()`) run the tool loop internally (`chat_impl` / `chat_impl_async` in `R/chat.R`). There is currently **no callback that fires before each model request inside that loop**, so an application cannot inspect or rewrite the conversation **between tool rounds** within a single `chat()` call.

The existing `on_tool_request(callback(request))` and `on_tool_result(callback(result))` hooks are tool-scoped: they receive only the request/result, don't fire when a turn has no tools (or before the first request), and there is no documented/safe contract for mutating `private$.turns` from them.

### Use case: mid-loop context compaction

I'm building an R coding agent on ellmer. To stay within the model's context window I need **automatic compaction between tool rounds** — exactly what Claude Code does by calling `autoCompactIfNeeded()` at the top of each iteration of its query loop. Because the tool loop is internal to ellmer, I can only compact **before** handing off to `chat()` (i.e. at user-turn boundaries). A single turn that triggers many large tool outputs (e.g. reading several big files) can blow the context limit mid-loop, with no opportunity to compact until the turn ends.

### Where it would hook

In `chat_impl` / `chat_impl_async`, at the top of `while (!is.null(user_turn)) { ... }`, before `private$submit_turns(user_turn, ...)`.

### Proposed API (sketch — happy to follow your preferred shape)

A callback fired before each model request in the loop, mirroring the existing `CallbackManager` pattern:

```r
# fires before each submit_turns() inside the tool loop
cancel <- chat$on_turn_start(function() {
  # app can inspect/rewrite history here, e.g. compact:
  if (my_should_compact(chat)) chat$set_turns(my_compact(chat$get_turns()))
})
```

Naming/signature is entirely yours to decide (`on_turn_start` / `on_request` / a `turn_transform` that returns turns, etc.). The key need is a **safe, documented point to rewrite conversation history between tool rounds**.

### Alternatives considered

- `on_tool_result` + a captured `chat` to call `set_turns()`: works only by luck, is undocumented, doesn't fire without tools, and risks orphaning `tool_use`/`tool_result` pairs.
- Re-implementing the tool loop outside ellmer using lower-level primitives: `submit_turns()` is private, so there's no clean public way to drive one model turn + tools manually.

I'd be glad to send a PR if you're open to the feature — just let me know the API shape you'd prefer.

title: Feature Request: Allow custom `base_url` in `chat_google_vertex()` for API gateway proxies
body:
Note: Steps so far were run locally and final issue was created with assistance of Opus 4.6

## Problem

When using Google Vertex AI models through a corporate API gateway (Azure API Management),
the gateway proxies requests using Google's native API format
(`/v1beta1/publishers/google/models/{model}:generateContent`) with API key auth
(`x-goog-api-key` header).

Currently, `chat_google_vertex()` does not accept a `base_url` argument, so there's
no way to point it at a custom endpoint. The gateway is NOT OpenAI-compatible, so
`chat_openai_compatible()` doesn't work either.

## Workaround

Using `httr2` directly works:

```r
url <- "https://my-gateway.example.com/vertex-ai-express/v1beta1/publishers/google/models/gemini-2.5-flash-lite:generateContent"

resp <- request(url) |>
  req_headers(`x-goog-api-key` = api_key, `Content-Type` = "application/json") |>
  req_body_json(list(
    contents = list(list(role = "user", parts = list(list(text = "Hello!"))))
  )) |>
  req_perform()
```

The Python `google.genai` SDK supports this via `HttpOptions(base_url=...)`:

```python
from google.genai import Client
from google.genai.types import HttpOptions

client = Client(vertexai=True, api_key=api_key, http_options=HttpOptions(base_url=ENDPOINT))
```

## Proposed Solution
Add a `base_url` parameter to `chat_google_vertex()` that overrides the default Google endpoint URL, similar to how the Python SDK's `HttpOptions(base_url=...)` works.

This would also need to support API key authentication (via `x-goog-api-key header`) as an alternative to OAuth/service account credentials.

## Environment
* ellmer version: 0.4.1
* R version: [your R version]
* Gateway path format: /v1beta1/publishers/google/models/{model}:{method}
* Auth: x-goog-api-key header with API key

title: Tool definitions don't accept valid special characters for function names or arguments, such as "ñ"
body:
R functions that contain characters such as "ñ" (very common Spanish letter that produces a common problem in data science, as its used in the word _año_, meaning _year_) are completely valid in R, but they cause problems with `{ellmer}`

Lets create a basic function that has `ñ` in its name and in its argument:

```r
obtener_datos_por_año <- function(año = NULL) {
  
  require(dplyr)
  
  datos <- data.frame(
    año = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024),
    inversión = c(100, 150, 200, 250, 300),
    proyectos = c(5, 8, 12, 15, 18)
  )
  
  datos <- datos |> 
    filter(año == .env$año)
  
  return(datos)
}
```
The function simply filters data from a dataframe.

Try out the function and it will work fine:

```r
obtener_datos_por_año(año = 2022)
```

Now let's create a tool definition with `{ellmer}`:

```r
library(ellmer)

# Crear la herramienta ellmer
tool_obtener_datos <- ellmer::tool(
  obtener_datos_por_año,
  "Obtiene datos de inversión y proyectos, filtrados opcionalmente por año (2020-2024)",
  arguments = list(
    año = type_integer(description = "Año a filtrar, entre 2020 y 2024")
  )
)
```

We get the first error: `ñ` is not supported in a function name:
```
# Error in `ellmer::tool()`:
#   ! `name` must contain only letters, numbers, - and _.
```

We have to change the function name (let´s say `anio` instead of `año`) to get rid of the error.

Now let's provide the LLM with the function definition:

```r
chat <- chat_anthropic(
  model = "claude-haiku-4-5"
)

chat$register_tool(tool_obtener_datos)
```

No problem so far, but let's ask a question that requires the model to use the tool, specifically the argument with `ñ` in its name:

```
chat$chat("muéstrame los proyectos de 2020") # "show me projects from 2020"
```

We get another `ñ` related error:
```
# Error in `req_perform_connection()`:
#   ! HTTP 400 Bad Request.
# ℹ tools.0.custom.input_schema.properties: Property keys should match
# pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,64}$' [invalid_request_error]
# Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.
```

I believe some cautions were taken to validate proper function and argument names in `{ellmer}` but those leave some users having to modify their work in order to match the english alphabet.

title: Streaming ContentThinking chunks lack proper <thinking> tag boundaries
body:
## Current behavior

When streaming with `stream = "content"`, each `ContentThinking` chunk is yielded as an independent object. If you print or concatenate these (via `format()`), each fragment gets its own `<thinking>...</thinking>` wrapper:

```r
chat <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514")

stream <- chat$stream("Explain recursion", stream = "content")
coro::loop(for (chunk in stream) {
  cat(format(chunk))
})
```

Output:

```
<thinking>
The user wants an explanation
</thinking>
<thinking>
 of recursion. I should
</thinking>
<thinking>
 start with a simple definition...
</thinking>
Recursion is a technique where...
```

With `stream = "text"`, thinking text is yielded as bare strings indistinguishable from response text:

```r
stream <- chat$stream("Explain recursion", stream = "text")
coro::loop(for (chunk in stream) {
  cat(chunk)
})
```

Output:

```
The user wants an explanation of recursion. I should start with a simple definition...Recursion is a technique where...
```

No way to tell where thinking ended and the response began.

## Expected behavior

The streaming layer should emit `<thinking>` tags at the boundaries — once at the start of thinking, once at the end — so that concatenated output is well-formed:

For `stream = "text"`:
```
<thinking>
The user wants an explanation of recursion. I should start with a simple definition...
</thinking>

Recursion is a technique where...
```

For `stream = "content"`, the yielded objects stay the same (`ContentThinking` per chunk), but the echo/display output should show proper boundaries.

## Why this matters

Downstream consumers (like shinychat) that receive a stream and need to separate thinking from response content currently have to implement their own stateful tracking of `ContentThinking` objects, accumulate the thinking text, and reconstruct the tag boundaries themselves. If the stream already had correct boundaries in text mode, consumers could treat it as a text stream with well-formed `<thinking>` tags and parse accordingly — no type inspection needed.

title: Token Budget / Cap for Agentic Tool Call Loops
body:
**Describe the problem**
When running unsupervised/scheduled agentic workflows that involve tool calls, there is currently no built-in way to enforce an upper token limit on the full multi-turn loop. Without this, a runaway loop can consume far more tokens than intended with no mechanism to stop it gracefully.

**Desired behavior**
It would be useful to have a supported way to:
1. Set a hard token budget for the entire tool call loop, causing it to stop (and error/fail gracefully) if the limit is exceeded.
2. Optionally inject a system-level message (e.g. *"You are approaching your token limit — wrap up your response now"*) once a soft threshold is reached, giving the model a chance to return a partial result rather than hard-stopping.

**Use case**
Unsupervised scheduled reports with tool access, where cost/token control is a requirement to prevent silent runaway.

title: Support multi-turn conversation suffixes in `parallel_chat_structured()`
body:
### Problem

`parallel_chat_structured()` currently supports only a single user turn per parallel job. This is because `as_user_turns()` converts each element of `prompts` into one `UserTurn`, and `append_turns()` appends that single turn to the shared conversation history:

```r
# R/parallel-chat.R L192-199
user_turns <- as_user_turns(prompts)
existing <- chat$get_turns(include_system_prompt = TRUE)
conversations <- append_turns(list(existing), user_turns)
```

```r
# R/turns.R L219-231
as_user_turns <- function(prompts, ...) {
  turns <- map(seq_along(prompts), function(i) {
    as_user_turn(prompts[[i]], ...)
  })
  turns
}
```

There is no mechanism to supply a multi-turn conversation suffix (e.g., user → assistant → user) per parallel job. Workloads that require each parallel item to be its own short conversation — rather than a single prompt — must fall back to sequential `chat$chat_structured()` calls on separate `Chat` objects, losing the throughput benefit of the parallel API.

### Use case

Simulation-style and survey-style workflows where each parallel item naturally involves multiple turns before the structured extraction. For example, running 500 independent two-turn conversations in parallel:

- **Turn 1:** establish identity/context for a simulated respondent
- **Turn 2:** ask the rating/classification question
- **Return:** structured JSON response

Other examples include multi-step annotation pipelines and interview-style prompting where the model should condition on a short prior exchange before producing a structured answer.

### Proposed API

Allow each element of `prompts` to be either a string (current behaviour, one turn) or a list of strings (new, multi-turn suffix):

```r
parallel_chat_structured(
  chat = chat,
  prompts = list(
    # Job 1: two-turn conversation
    list("You are simulating a Democrat.", "Rate this statement from 0 to 100."),
    # Job 2: two-turn conversation
    list("You are simulating a Republican.", "Rate this statement from 0 to 100."),
    # Job 3: single-turn (backward compatible)
    "Rate this statement from 0 to 100."
  ),
  type = response_type
)
```

This would also apply to `parallel_chat()`, `parallel_chat_text()`, and `batch_chat_structured()` since they share the same `as_user_turns()` / `append_turns()` pipeline.

### Implementation notes

The main changes would likely be in:

- **`as_user_turns()`** (`R/turns.R`): detect when an element is a list of strings and return a list of `Turn` objects (alternating user/assistant) rather than a single `UserTurn`.
- **`append_turns()`** (`R/parallel-chat.R`): handle appending a sequence of turns rather than a single turn.
- **`parallel_chat_structured()`** (`R/parallel-chat.R`): the structured variant would need to issue multiple rounds of `parallel_turns()` calls, similar to how `parallel_chat()` already loops for tool calls.

### Not a bug

The current docs and API clearly treat `prompts` as single-turn inputs. This is a feature request to extend the parallel API to cover multi-turn workloads.

_Originally raised in https://github.com/rempsyc/ellmer/issues/4._

title: Feature Request: Implement Native "Agent" Class (ReAct Loop) for Autonomous Workflows
body:
he Problem: Lack of Autonomy
Currently, `ellmer` provides an excellent interface for one-shot or interactive chat. However, it lacks a native mechanism for autonomy.

To execute multi-step tasks (e.g., "Download this CSV, clean it, and plot the trend"), a user currently has to manually act as the "runtime"—copying code blocks, executing them, and pasting errors back into the chat. There is no persistent object capable of the ReAct (Reason + Act) pattern to handle this loop automatically.

 The Proposed Solution
I propose implementing a dedicated `Agent` class (likely an R6 object) that wraps the existing `Chat` interface to enable autonomous execution.

1. The `Agent` Class (The Brain)
A stateful object that manages a `while` loop of  Thought → Action → Observation.
* It would leverage the existing `chat` object for LLM calls.
* It would automatically handle context window management and recursion limits (`max_steps`).
* User Experience:
  ```r
  agent <- Agent$new(chat)
  agent$run("Analyze this dataset")

2. Strict Tool Interface Current tool definitions are flexible, but an Agent needs strict contracts. I propose a Tool class that:
* Wraps R functions (e.g., read.csv, ggplot).
* Automatically generates the JSON schema required by OpenAI/Anthropic (extracting params from formals()).
* Handles execution errors gracefully, feeding them back to the LLM for self-correction.

3. Safety & Sandboxing (Crucial) Autonomy requires safety. The Agent would include:
* File System Jail: Restricting I/O to a specific subdirectory (e.g., ./agent_scratchpad/).
* Human-in-the-Loop: A confirm_execution = TRUE mode where the user approves tools before they run.

Implementation Details
I have spent time analyzing ellmer's internals (specifically during my work on PR #906 regarding chat history architecture) and believe this can be implemented as a clean layer on top of the existing providers.

GSoC 2026 Participation
I have drafted a complete 5-page Technical Specification (including architecture diagrams and a 12-week timeline) for building this feature.

I would love to champion this implementation as a Google Summer of Code 2026 project.

Question for Maintainers: Is ellmer (or the Tidyverse team) considering participating in GSoC this year?

If so, I am ready to share the full proposal immediately. If not, I am still keen to discuss this design for future community contributions!

body:
If you have a long or large chat conversation, the print method (i.e. what's shown in the console) can be quite large and can even overflow the console buffer.

In particular, it can be hard to find the chat summary with cost, tokens and turn counts when the chat is quite large. It might be nice to update the print method -- or to add a `summary()` method? -- that collapses turns into a summary view and shows just high-level information.

New Feature Request : Custom metadata labels - Vertex A
body:
Hi Team,

Request your support to add Custom metadata label while accessing gemini models in Vertex AI.

Business Need:

(Source Reference : https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/multimodal/add-labels-to-api-calls)
What are labels?
A label is a key-value pair that you can assign to generateContent and streamGenerateContent API calls. They help you organize these calls and manage your costs at scale, with the granularity you need. You can attach a label to each call, then filter the calls based on their labels. Information about labels is forwarded to the billing system that lets you break down your billed charges by label. With built-in [billing reports](https://cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/reports), you can filter and group costs by labels.

Common use cases for labels
Team or cost center labels: Add labels based on team or cost center to distinguish API calls owned by different teams (for example, team:research and team:analytics). You can use this type of label for cost accounting or budgeting.
Component labels: For example, component:redis, component:frontend, component:ingest, and component:dashboard.
Environment or stage labels: For example, environment:production and environment:test.
Ownership labels: Used to identify the teams that are responsible for operations, for example: team:shopping-cart.

R Code to access via REST API

```R
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)

# ---- STEP 1: Set your values ----
project_id <- "your-project-id"            # <-- Replace with your GCP project ID
location <- "us-central1"                  # <-- Replace with region (e.g., us-central1)
model_id <- "gemini-1.5-pro-preview-0409"  # <-- Replace with your model ID
response_method <- "generateContent"       # or "streamGenerateContent"

# Prompt and labels
prompt_text <- "What are the key benefits of using generative AI in financial services?"
label_key <- "env"
label_value <- "test"

# ---- STEP 2: Get access token from gcloud ----
access_token <- system("gcloud auth print-access-token", intern = TRUE)

# ---- STEP 3: Prepare request body ----
body <- list(
  contents = list(
    role = "USER",
    parts = list(text = prompt_text)
  ),
  labels = setNames(list(label_value), label_key)
)

# ---- STEP 4: Convert to JSON ----
json_body <- toJSON(body, auto_unbox = TRUE)

# ---- STEP 5: Make POST request ----
url <- sprintf("https://%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/%s/locations/%s/publishers/google/models/%s:%s",
               location, project_id, location, model_id, response_method)

res <- POST(
  url,
  add_headers(
    Authorization = paste("Bearer", access_token),
    `Content-Type` = "application/json; charset=utf-8"
  ),
  body = json_body
)

# ---- STEP 6: View the response ----
cat(content(res, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))
```

title: Have a debugging story for credentials
body:
Now that we do so much magic internally to get ambient credentials, I wonder if we need better ways to surface (and/or debug) what credentials have been selected to users.

Something like the following:

```r
> chat <- chat_snowflake()
## Using model = "llama3.1-70b".
## Using key-pair authentication.
```

or

```r
> chat <- chat_databricks()
## Using machine-to-machine (M2M) credentials.
```

or

```r
> chat <- chat_azure()
## Using Azure service principal credentials.
```

Of course, that might be annoying if we print it every time; I know that `gargle` at least has a "verbosity" setting that turns on debug messages for the credential source. The internal API could be:

```r
set_auth_source <- function(src) {
  if (!getOption("ellmer_auth_debug", FALSE)) {
    return()
  }
  cli::cli_inform("Using {.field {src}}.")
}
```
